summary: Disabled buttons in the toolbar's pills are drawn dimmed: Back and Forward with nowhere to go, and Search Only in This Folder where the window shows no single folder (Recents, the Trash, sent results). src/finder/toolbar.rs: `pill_button` no longer sets a text colour. The kit (gpui-component-0.8.1 button/button.rs) lays a button's own style over its colours at rest and replays it inside its selected and disabled state styles, so the colour `pill_button` set took the place of the kit's disabled colour. Without it a ghost button is drawn in `secondary.foreground` at rest, pressed and selected, in `accent.foreground` under the mouse (as before: the hover and pressed styles always sat over the button's own), and in `muted.foreground` at half opacity when disabled. In both bundled themes the first two equal `foreground`, so only disabled buttons look different. `pill_button(id, icon)` and `menu_button(id, icon)` no longer take `cx`, which they took only to read that colour; every caller is updated (toolbar.rs, and Hide Sidebar in src/finder/sidebar.rs). docs/manual.md: the Toolbar table's Back, Forward row and its Search Only in "Folder name" row say the buttons are dimmed.
changelog: Back and Forward in the toolbar are dimmed while they have nowhere to go, and Search Only in This Folder is dimmed in Recents, the Trash, and other places that aren't one folder. They were drawn like buttons that can be pressed, so a new window showed a Back and a Forward that looked ready to use.
behaviour_changes: Back and Forward are drawn dimmed while they are disabled, which is while they have nowhere to go: both in a new window, Forward after going into a folder, Back after going back to where the window opened. Before, they were drawn in the full text colour, the same as enabled ones. Measured in pictures: light theme, icon (191,191,191) on the pill's white where an enabled one is (38,38,38); dark theme, (105,105,105) on (48,48,48) where an enabled one is (224,224,224).

Search Only in This Folder is drawn dimmed where it is disabled: Recents and the Trash (pictured), and by the same line of code any other place that is not one folder. With the choice on, it is drawn dimmed and not selected there, and on again back in a folder (probed and pictured).

The dimming is the one the window's other disabled buttons have (Empty… over an empty Trash measures (188,188,188) on (251,251,251) and (103,103,103) on (45,45,45)): the theme's muted colour at half opacity. Disabled menu items are stronger; they use the muted colour whole.

The same holds in each pane of split view, in a window with tabs, in a narrow toolbar, with the sidebar hidden (all pictured, both themes) and in a file chooser (probed in a headless test), which all draw the same toolbar.

During a search in a window that has been nowhere else Back is enabled (since back-forward-restore-search). It now looks it, beside a dimmed Forward. Escape makes it dimmed again; Back ends the search and Forward is then the enabled one (probed).
A button that becomes disabled under the pointer (a click on Back that reaches the start) is dimmed at once and has no hover background (pictured).

Nothing else changes. Buttons that can be pressed look as they did at rest, under the mouse, pressed, selected, with their menu open and with the keyboard on them. Which buttons are disabled, what a click does, the tooltips (Back to "name" on an enabled one, plain Back with its key on a disabled one), the right-click menus (none on a disabled one) and the Tab order (Tab skipped a disabled button before too; now it can be seen why) are untouched.

docs/manual.md: the Toolbar table's Back, Forward row gains "Back or Forward is dimmed while it has nowhere to go.", and the Search Only in "Folder name" row reads "It's off, and dimmed, in Recents and other results that aren't one folder."
left_out: CHANGELOG.md is not edited, per the guide. The entry is in this record and in the commit message.

The tab bar's and the bars' buttons, which the brief asked to check for the same fault: nothing to fix. No other button builder chain in src sets a text colour or an opacity of its own (my own scan of every `Button::new`, `pill_button`, `menu_button` and `pdf_button` chain, 81 of them, and by eye every control with a `.disabled(..)`: Kind, Choose, Empty…, Clear, the text-size and settings steppers, the terminal picker, the PDF pager and zoom). The tab bar's + and × are plain divs that are never disabled.

No test reads the colour of the real toolbar's buttons: the harness's element snapshot has no style. The unit test reads the colour inside a button made by `pill_button`, so a colour set on a pill button at a call site would get past it. `pill_button`'s comment says so.

The kept unit test asserts the colour at rest, selected and disabled. Under the mouse and pressed were checked in review by a throwaway test (equal to the text colour in both themes) and, for the mouse, in pictures.
How strong the dimming is was not tuned: it is the kit's for every disabled button. See the doubts in notes.

The Linux window buttons fffinder draws where the window manager draws none (Minimize, Maximize, Close) are pill buttons too, never disabled; the screenshot example draws no such window, so they were not pictured.
`cargo clippy --features term` was not run: nothing in src/term calls the changed functions (grepped), which is the guide's condition for it.
Nothing was compiled or run for macOS or Windows.
tests: src/finder/toolbar.rs: finder::toolbar::tests::a_disabled_pill_button_is_drawn_dimmed_in_both_themes. It draws a pill button in a test window and reads the text colour inside it, which is the colour the icon takes: the theme's foreground at rest and selected, and for a disabled one the colour the kit gives its own disabled ghost button. Without the change it fails at `assert_eq!(disabled, kits)` in Light, left alpha 0.851 against right 0.251 (run in review on the old code, with the test adapted to the old three-argument `pill_button`). A colour set in `pill_button` again fails it too.

tests/controls.rs: toolbar_buttons_that_would_do_nothing_are_disabled. Back, Forward and Search Only in This Folder in a new window, a folder further, back again, and in Recents. It passes without the change as well: it pins the disabled state that the dimming follows, which was the brief's fallback. Mutations caught in review: `.disabled(..)` taken off Back or off Forward (fails at 'in a new window'), off the scope button (fails at 'in Recents').
review_fixes: src/finder/toolbar.rs: `pill_button`'s comment now says that a colour set on the button by a caller does what one set in the function did: it replaces the kit's colours, the disabled one with them. That is the one way the fault can come back with every test passing, and briefs still to come add buttons to the toolbar.
Nothing else. I found nothing to correct in the implementer's code, tests, manual text or commit message.
notes:
Checked. check.sh printed CHECK OK on the tree of the trunk commit: 611 passed in 16 test binaries, 3 of 3 known root-only failures (the trunk had 609). The trunk did not move during the review, so there was nothing to rebase onto: the trunk commit is the implementer's 59dac20 with the comment fix above folded in. My own `git push origin search-ui-polish` was denied twice by this session's permission system ("Destructive or Unwanted Actions"), the second time sent alone after `git status` as the refusal allowed, and I did not look for another way. The commit reached origin all the same with the next integration: table-preview-scroll went onto the trunk on top of it minutes later and its push went through, so the fork's search-ui-polish is at 66d4fad, which contains c28f42d (read back with `git ls-remote`).

How it was checked. (1) The cause, in the kit's source: gpui-component button/button.rs lays `instance_style` over the normal colours (`refine_style(&instance_style)`) and replays it inside `styles.selected` and `styles.disabled`; gpui-base button.rs resolves base, then selected, then disabled, and puts hover and active over that as the div's own hover and active styles. (2) Without the change: with the src diff reverse-applied and the unit test put back in a form the old three-argument `pill_button` takes, it fails as described under tests; the UI test passes on the old code, by design. Four mutations of the new code, one at a time, each failed a kept test (a colour set in `pill_button`; `.disabled(..)` taken off Back, off Forward, off the scope button). Both tests and their neighbours pass under SEED 0, 3, 17 and 1234 and in 15 iterations. (3) Pictures of my own, the same 26 shots in both themes on the old code and on the new, compared pixel by pixel (52 pairs): a new window, a folder further, back again, a search, Search Only in This Folder on, Recents, the Trash, the mouse on a view button, on a disabled Back, on an enabled Back, on Show Sidebar and on Hide Sidebar, the Sort, View and Actions menus open, split view, a 700 pt window, two tabs, list view, the sidebar hidden (a new window and a folder further), and the keyboard on a toolbar button after one, two and three Tab presses in a new window and after three a folder further. One shot, taken with `--no-sidebar`, turned out to be a second new window (see Found, not fixed). In every pair the only pixels that differ are the icons of the disabled buttons, and the status bar's free-space figure or search time. (4) Throwaway tests, deleted: the colour inside an enabled, a selected and a disabled pill button at rest, under the mouse and pressed, in both themes (enabled and selected equal the text colour in all three; disabled is the dimmed colour in all three), and with the theme's `secondary.foreground` and `accent.foreground` set apart to see which each state takes (rest and pressed the first, hover the second). The buttons' disabled state through a search started and ended with Escape, ended with Back and returned to with Forward; through the Trash and Recents with Search Only in This Folder on, a click on the disabled button (changes nothing), and back; in both panes of split view (each has its own); in a file chooser; in a 640 pt window. (5) Six pictures of mine are kept (review-1 to review-6); I looked at the implementer's montages and close-up as well.

The three ways I thought this most likely to hurt someone, and what the code says. (1) A dimmed button too faint to find, or dimmed unlike the rest of the window. It is the kit's disabled colour, `muted.foreground` at half opacity, the same ink as Empty… over an empty Trash (measured, see behaviour_changes). Against the pill that is about 1.8 to 1 in the light theme and 2.4 to 1 in the dark one: faint, plainly visible at full size in both, and about what Finder's own disabled Back has. (2) A button that can be pressed looking different, or looking disabled. Only a `.disabled(true)` button takes the disabled style, and the kit makes such a button inert and takes it out of the Tab order, so dimmed and can't-be-pressed cannot come apart; the three `.disabled(..)` are computed in render_toolbar from the same lists as the tooltips and menus, and the probes found them right in every place I tried. For the buttons that can be pressed, the hover and pressed colours never came from `pill_button` (the kit lays them over a button's own style), and rest and selected now come from `secondary.foreground`, which both bundled themes set to the same value as `foreground`; no theme files are loaded from anywhere else, and the macOS accent substitution in src/theme.rs replaces only `#007AFF` values and the table's selection colour. The unit test pins rest and selected to the theme's foreground, so a theme edit that separates them fails it. The scope button cannot be selected and disabled at once (`in_folder` requires a folder). (3) The branch no longer building, or its tests failing, on the owner's Mac or on Windows. `pill_button` and `menu_button` lost a parameter: `git grep` over the whole repository finds callers only in toolbar.rs and sidebar.rs, none under a `cfg` attribute, in src/term, src/macos.rs, src/win.rs, examples or tests, and toolbar.rs still uses everything it imports. The UI test is the first to call `ElementSnapshot::disabled()`; the flag is written by the kit's test-support wrapper from the element's own accessibility info during prepaint (gpui-base a11y_disabled.rs, test_support.rs), with no platform accessibility tree involved, and the kit's own test pins `Some(true)` / `None`. The unit test's setup (`gpui_kit::init`, `theme::install`, `theme::apply`) is the one views.rs's `drag_frames_set_a_readable_text_color_in_both_themes` already uses on all three systems.

For the briefs still to come.
- Any brief that adds or moves a button in the toolbar or the sidebar's top (recent-searches, split-view-toolbar-clip, split-active-pane, smart-folder-save-and-leaks): `pill_button(id, icon)` and `menu_button(id, icon)` take two arguments now; a call with `cx` no longer compiles. Do not set a text colour on a pill button, in the function or at the call (`.text_color(..)` on the Button): the kit replays a button's own style inside its disabled style, so the button would stop looking disabled. A `.disabled(true)` kit button is dimmed with nothing more to do. An `Icon` given its own colour ignores the button's colours in every state.
- recent-searches: your `Button::new("search-history").ghost().xsmall().icon(IconName::Search)` replaces a prefix icon that is drawn in `muted_foreground` through `.text_color(..)` on the Icon. Keep the colour on the Icon if you want that look; on the Button it would be replayed into every state. If you fall back to a pill beside the field, see the item above.
- split-active-pane: the title's `muted_foreground` in an inactive pane (your `.when(split && !active, ..)` on the title div) does not reach the pill buttons, and a colour set on a toolbar ancestor would not either: the kit sets each button's colour itself. An inactive pane's enabled buttons stay in the full text colour beside its muted title and its dimmed, disabled Back and Forward. For your Tab work: a disabled kit button is not a tab stop, so the Tab ring changes with the history. In a new window Tab goes from Hide Sidebar straight to the first view button; with somewhere to go back to it takes one press more, Back being a stop (review-5).
- split-view-toolbar-clip: in pictures of a new window both Back and Forward are dimmed, and so is Search Only in This Folder in Recents and the Trash. That is this change, not a drawing fault. The toolbar's widths and the fold are untouched (the measuring test in tests/basics.rs passes). `the_toolbar_folds_one_step_at_a_time` is still the first test in toolbar.rs's test module; the new colour test and its two helpers follow it.
- search-settings-hints-steppers: your plan draws a stepper's value as a disabled button when it is at its default, so that most people see all four values dimmed. Measured here, a disabled ghost button's content is (191,191,191) on white in the light theme and (105,105,105) on (48,48,48) in the dark one, about 1.8 to 1 and 2.4 to 1. That suits a glyph on a button that can't be pressed; it is hard on a value someone has to read. Look at it in both themes. If the value should stay readable while disabled, a `.text_color(..)` on that Button does it, by the very mechanism this change took out of the pill buttons.
- inactive-selection-colour: for a test that pins a colour as drawn, `Inked` and `ink` in toolbar.rs's test module show one way: a view whose element gets a `canvas` child that records `window.text_style().color`, drawn with `add_window_view` and `render_frame`. It reads what an element's children inherit, at rest; for hover and pressed see the checks above.
- empty-state-messages, collapsed-groups-empty-view, smart-folder-save-and-leaks, show-in-enclosing-folder-key: `ui.snapshot(id).disabled()` is `Some(true)` for a disabled kit control and `None` for an enabled one, on every system; the comment in `back_and_forward_buttons` that said buttons report no such state was out of date and is corrected. `ui.snapshot(id).selected()` is `None` for a kit Button drawn selected (a view button, the scope button): `.selected(true)` is how it looks, not accessibility state, so read the Finder's own state for that.
- restore-session-tabs: a restored tab starts with no history, so its Back and Forward are dimmed until it goes somewhere.
- context-menus-fit, focus-lost-recovery, go-to-folder-keyboard, type-select-space, select-all-perf, preview-card-height, tab-bar-overflow: nothing but line numbers. In src/finder/toolbar.rs everything after `pill_button` is three lines further down and the test module has sixty-four more lines ahead of `a_history_buttons_tooltip_names_where_it_leads`; in tests/controls.rs everything after `view_buttons_switch_views` is twenty-one lines further down (the new test sits between it and `back_and_forward_buttons`).
- Anyone taking pictures: see the first item under Found, not fixed.

Found, not fixed (there before, outside this brief).
- `--no-sidebar` of examples/screenshot.rs, and so of shot.sh, leaves the sidebar showing (seen on the old code and the new). `--do key:ctrl-alt-s` hides it. The example calls `set_sidebar_visible`, which changes the tab's copy of the setting without publishing it; I did not trace what puts it back.
- The window has two strengths of unavailable: a disabled button is the muted colour at half opacity, a disabled menu item the muted colour whole. Both are the kit's.
- The harness cannot tell whether a kit Button is drawn selected (see the briefs above), so no UI test holds that the current view's button or the scope button looks on.
- After a right-click on a disabled Back or Forward the plain tooltip shows, since the pointer rests on the button (review-4). history-menus' pictures show the same.

Doubts that remain, for the owner. (a) How strong the dimming should be. It is the kit's standard and matches every other disabled button in the window and, roughly, Finder; in the light theme it is a light grey chevron on white. If it should be stronger, `.when(disabled, |b| b.text_color(cx.theme().muted_foreground))` at the three calls that disable (Back, Forward, the scope button) gives the strength disabled menu items have. (b) Nothing ran on macOS or Windows. On a Mac check once, in light and dark: a new window's Back and Forward are dimmed, and with an accent colour other than blue the toolbar's buttons look as before. (c) The look of the buttons that can be pressed now follows the theme's `secondary.foreground` and `accent.foreground`, equal to `foreground` today. An edit of assets/themes/fffinder.json that separates them changes the pill buttons, where the old override hid it at rest and when selected; the unit test then fails and says which. (d) The manual says "dimmed", a word it had not used; elsewhere it says "disabled" for the Kind menu and "unavailable" for Put Back. (e) The UI test does not fail without the change and the unit test cannot see a colour set at a call site; the pictures are what show the real toolbar.

Housekeeping. My temporary files were in lane-f-disabled-toolbar-buttons-look in the shared scratchpad, which I deleted; I touched nothing else there. The probes were a throwaway tests/zz_probe_disabled.rs and a throwaway test in toolbar.rs's module, both removed before the check; after each reverse-apply and mutation the source files were compared byte for byte with saved copies of the commit's. The lane is clean and at the trunk's tip.
